answer: The MVP gives your agents a Linux main computer on your Mac, reached over SSH by the terminal, editor and agent programs you already use, with full access inside and sign-in opening in your Mac's browser. Outside the computer, Silo runs the Zig engine behind one versioned API, owns the network boundary with open, limited or closed modes, swaps plain secret placeholders at the boundary so real values never enter the computer or the record, keeps an append-only record of facts and reports, takes APFS copy-on-write disk checkpoints with restore and forks, compares file changes between checkpoints, and reads model calls at the boundary. You drive every MVP feature from a views-only Swift Mac app without touching the command line, including entering secrets outside any chat and copying or exporting a full receipt with its record and file diffs to hand to an agent for analysis, while the `silo` command on your Mac drives the same API as plain text or JSON lines. Tools inside computers, a macOS main, the extension runtime, classifiers, precautions, held requests, Nix recipes, non-swap secrets (SSH signing, OAuth exchanges and cloud signing) and spend budgets come after MVP.
